ground_truth_root_cause: The backbone router configuration push (job_id=cfg-push-20240312-0001), triggered by the automated job scheduled in commit f0a2c4e6b813, deployed a bundled config assembled in commit e9f1b3d5a724. This bundle contained two critical errors introduced across commits 7f2a0c4e8d16 and d4e6a8b0c312: (1) The BGP peer MD5 authentication keys in bgp-peers.conf were rotated to new values that did not yet match what upstream transit providers had configured, causing all BGP sessions to be rejected immediately upon config push. (2) The refactored ACL ruleset in backbone-router-acl.conf placed the catch-all deny-all rule before the explicit permit rules due to a merge ordering error, causing all transit traffic to be dropped at the ACL level even if BGP had recovered. Both errors combined caused all four backbone routers to simultaneously withdraw all BGP-advertised prefixes, resulting in a complete global network partition and 100% service unavailability across all dependent services.
ground_truth_remediation: Immediately roll back the backbone router configuration to the last known-good config snapshot (cfg-push-20240312-0000) using the router-config-mgmt tooling rollback command targeting all four backbone routers. Once BGP sessions re-establish and routing tables converge (expected within 60-90 seconds per router), verify all BGP sessions are active and all prefixes re-advertised. Then correct the ACL rule ordering in backbone-router-acl.conf so permit rules precede deny-all, and coordinate with upstream transit providers to synchronize BGP peer MD5 keys before any subsequent push. Add mandatory integration and simulation tests to the CI pipeline for backbone config changes and require a staged canary rollout to a single non-critical router before global push.
